家計調査報告 1937–38

Kakei chōsa hōkoku (Report of the Household Budget Survey), 自昭和十二年十一月至昭和十三年十月 (November 1937 – October 1938)
臺灣總督官房企畫部 (Planning Department, Secretariat of the Government-General of Taiwan), 臺北, 1940 (昭和15年3月)

Every table is transcribed: the small tables of the survey outline, the in-text tables of the summary of results, and the statistical tables 第一表–第七表 for Japanese and for Taiwanese households (第五表–第七表 for the whole island and each of the nine cities), with the classification of income and expenditure; the prose and the account-book forms are not. Each spread was read once by Claude Sonnet 5.5 from tight crops (Arabic figures); two missions that had read from half-page views were read again from scratch. The large island-wide tables run over several spreads, each spread carrying half the columns for one block of rows: the pieces read by different readers are joined into one table per printed table, with amounts (實數) and percentages (比例) as separate parts, and a check that no cell was lost or doubled. Decimal points printed as spaces, hyphens, commas or raised dots, and zeros printed as a broken 'C', are written as normal figures and noted. The errata slip (正誤表, 20 corrections) is attached as a note to each table it concerns; the figures stay as printed. Where a digit was ambiguous only between 3 and 8 and exactly one reading made a printed total reconcile, that reading is used and noted; printed totals that do not add up are kept as printed and noted. Cells the first reader could not make out in tables with more than four such cells were read again blind by Claude Opus 5.5 (271 of 533 filled; readings the second reader itself marked doubtful were not used). 351 of about 189,000 filled cells could not be read and are marked [?].
